channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: BlackRock Identifies Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan as Emerging Investment Hubs
item.description: BlackRock Investment Institute views Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan as increasingly attractive destinations for international capital, alongside India and Gulf states. Reforms in Kazakhstan, including pension and capital market changes, are noted as key drivers of this interest.

item.title: Chinese Company Plans Production at Kolzhat Deposit in Kazakhstan
item.description: Xinfa Group, a Chinese corporation, is preparing a project for the comprehensive development of the Kolzhat coal deposit in the Almaty region, aiming to create approximately two thousand jobs. Kazakhstan's President discussed the project's prospects with Xinfa Group's president.

item.title: Russian State Media Published and Deleted Article Threatening Lithuania with Nuclear Strike
item.description: Russian state news agency RIA Novosti published an article suggesting a "small special military operation" and nuclear strike on Lithuania, which was later deleted. The article discussed a scenario of missile strikes on Lithuania and was attributed to an editor with alleged ties to Russian administration.

item.title: Head of Kyrgyzaltyn Inspects Progress at Togolok Gold Deposit Development
item.description: The chairman of Kyrgyzaltyn, Kubat Abd Raimov, visited the Togolok gold deposit to review mining, exploration, and infrastructure construction. He emphasized the project's importance for Kyrgyzstan's mining sector, noting its reliance on domestic specialists and funding. Environmental and safety standards were highlighted.

item.title: Vice-Admiral Explains Caspian Sea Tragedy: Simple Exercise, Unpredictable Conditions
item.description: Former Naval Commander Vice-Admiral Zhandarbek Zhanzakov discussed the Caspian Sea tragedy, explaining how weather can rapidly change at sea, impacting even simple exercises. He noted that ship commanders decide on deployments based on forecasts, but conditions can shift from 2 m/s to 20 m/s wind within an hour.

item.title: Kaspi Bank to Pay Shareholders Nearly 75 Billion Tenge in Dividends
item.description: Kaspi Bank shareholders approved a dividend payout of 4,000 tenge per share for 2025. The total payout will be approximately 74.8 billion tenge, based on the number of outstanding shares. This follows a previous dividend payment of 1,600 tenge per share earlier in 2026.

item.title: Robotics production plant for educational and service robots to open in Almaty
item.description: A plant for the production of educational and service robots by UBTECH Robotics is planned to launch in Almaty. The project was discussed by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and company president Zhong Yong. Kazakhstan will be the company's first production site outside China, facilitating partnerships in education and technology integration.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China establish joint investment fund for new projects
item.description: Kazakhstan and China are establishing a specialized investment fund to finance new projects in Kazakhstan, operating through the Astana International Financial Centre. An agreement was signed by Kazakh Invest and Silk Road Finance Corporation at the Kazakhstan-China Investment Forum in Almaty. Bilateral trade reached $48.7 billion in 2025.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan prepares to launch its first domestically developed satellite in early October
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to launch its first domestically developed satellite in early October to collect imagery of farmland, pastures, glaciers, and water resources. The spacecraft, developed by state-owned Kyrgyz Asman, will aid in assessing crop conditions, detecting drought, and monitoring water resources and emergency areas.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China to establish automotive production complex in East Kazakhstan region
item.description: A memorandum was signed between the East Kazakhstan region and a Chinese entrepreneur to create a joint venture, TOО East Motors Corporation. The project aims to establish a production complex for cars and specialized equipment, creating up to 500 jobs. Production will evolve from assembly to a full technological cycle, with a potential output of 80,000 vehicles annually and a localization level of 50%.

item.title: Robot technology plant to open in Almaty with support from President Tokayev
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with UBTECH Robotics Corp. to discuss cooperation in robotics, education, and AI. Tokayev supported the company's plan to open a robot production plant in Almaty, which will be its first manufacturing site outside China. The project aligns with agreements made in Shanghai and aims to foster collaboration with Kazakh technical universities.

item.title: Kazakh Defense Minister comments on Caspian Sea tragedy, vows accountability
item.description: Kazakhstan's Defense Minister has made his first public statement following the Caspian Sea tragedy, stating that "we will not evade responsibility." The minister's comments indicate a commitment to addressing the aftermath of the incident and ensuring accountability for those involved.

item.title: Kazakh Defense Minister Expresses Condolences Over Caspian Sea Tragedy
item.description: Kazakhstan's Defense Minister Dauren Kosanov stated that those responsible for the deaths of 14 servicemen in the Caspian Sea will be held accountable. He expressed deep condolences to the families and assured them of necessary assistance. The incident occurred during naval exercises when 17 servicemen were swept into the sea due to a sudden storm.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Climate Cooperation Initiatives at UN General Assembly
item.description: Eldor Aripov, Director of the Institute for Strategic and Regional Studies, presented proposals for developing international climate cooperation at the UN General Assembly in New York. He highlighted climate change as a driver for regional cooperation, particularly in Central Asia, where water, food, and energy security are interconnected.

item.title: Uzbekistan and EU to Discuss Trans-Caspian Corridor Investments and Border Facilitation
item.description: Tashkent will host a conference on the Trans-Caspian transport corridor, focusing on investments in rail and road infrastructure, digitalization of transport documents, and border crossing facilitation. The event, co-organized by Uzbekistan's Ministry of Transport and the European Commission, aims to coordinate projects within the EU's Global Gateway strategy.

item.title: Kazakhstan Investigates Commanders After 14 Servicemen Die in Caspian Military Drills
item.description: Fourteen Kazakh servicemen died and five officials were detained during Caspian Sea military exercises on September 24. A criminal case was opened for negligence and navigation rule violations. September 25 was declared a day of national mourning. The Khazar Qorgany 2026 exercises involved over 500 personnel and various naval and air units.

item.title: Second Survivor of Caspian Sea Tragedy: What is Known?
item.description: Details are emerging about the second serviceman who survived the recent tragedy in the Caspian Sea. The incident, which occurred during military exercises, resulted in multiple fatalities. Information regarding the survivor's condition and the circumstances of his rescue is being gathered.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Sadyr Japarov Schedules Presidential Elections
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan has officially announced the date for the upcoming presidential elections. The decree sets the election for a future date, marking a significant step in the country's political calendar. Further details regarding the election campaign are expected.

item.title: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev Meets with Xinfa Group President
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with the president of Xinfa Group, expressing Kazakhstan's interest in working with large investors committed to long-term cooperation, technology transfer, and industrial development. Discussions included the potential development of the Kolzhat deposit in the Almaty region and strengthening partnerships in critical materials.

item.title: Around 100 driver's licenses illegally issued in Nooen district, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Authorities in Kyrgyzstan's Jalal-Abad region uncovered the illegal issuance of approximately 100 driver's licenses in the Nooen district. Officials allegedly took bribes to falsify records in the driver registry system. Two individuals, an official and an intermediary, have been detained.

item.title: Man previously convicted of murder and rape detained on new charges in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A man previously convicted of murder and rape has been detained in Kyrgyzstan in connection with a new case involving the illegal acquisition and possession of drugs, as well as threats against close relatives. Further details are expected.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Link Agricultural Subsidies to Performance from 2025
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to transition to a "results-based subsidy" model in agriculture starting next year, shifting from a "funding allocation" approach. Subsidies will be tied to specific outcomes like yield, water and energy efficiency, and resource utilization. This new mechanism will initially be tested for water-saving technologies.

item.title: Uzbek President and Georgian Prime Minister Hold Phone Conversation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze held a phone conversation. Mirziyoyev congratulated Kobakhidze on his birthday. They discussed expanding Uzbek-Georgian strategic partnership, focusing on practical implementation of agreements from Mirziyoyev's July visit to Georgia, increasing trade, industrial cooperation, and transport connectivity.

item.title: Kazakh Parliamentarians Donate Over 146 Million Tenge to Families of Deceased and Injured Soldiers
item.description: Deputies of the Kurultai will transfer over 146 million tenge to the families of deceased and injured servicemen. The decision follows a tragedy in the Mangystau region. A voluntary collection was organized, with individual deputies contributing significant sums.

item.title: International Tourism Exhibition Opens in Dushanbe
item.description: The Dushanbe-2026 International Tourism Exhibition opened on September 24 in Dushanbe. The event aims to promote Tajikistan's tourism potential, attract foreign tourists, and foster international cooperation. Over 115 companies from 22 countries are participating.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China Sign Investment Agreements at Almaty Forum
item.description: During an investment forum in Almaty, Kazakhstan and China signed several documents. Agreements include building an aluminum plant and a wind power station in Abai region, a wood chipboard plant in Semey, and establishing an investment fund for projects in Kazakhstan.

item.title: Twelve Servicemen Die During Military Exercises in Kazakhstan's Mangystau Region
item.description: Twelve servicemen lost their lives on September 24 during military exercises conducted by the armed forces of Kazakhstan in the Mangystau region. Kazakh authorities reported the incident occurred during training drills.

item.title: Political Party 'Adilet' to Allocate 1.5 Billion Tenge to Families of Deceased Caspian Servicemen
item.description: The political party 'Adilet' and its Business Council will donate 1.5 billion tenge to aid families of servicemen killed or injured during naval exercises in the Caspian Sea. This initiative follows a tragedy where 14 soldiers died and three were rescued.

item.title: Mangystau Akimat States Forcing Donations for Fallen Soldiers' Families is Unacceptable
item.description: The Akimat of the Mangystau region has declared that forcing donations for the families of soldiers who died during exercises is unacceptable. The Akimat emphasized that contributions to the fund are voluntary and no instructions have been issued to citizens or organizations. Two criminal cases have been initiated following the incident where 14 soldiers died at sea.

item.title: Former Kyrgyz Interior Minister Plans Presidential Run
item.description: The former head of Kyrgyzstan's Interior Ministry has announced his intention to run for president. He previously served as the minister of internal affairs in the country.

item.title: Turkmenistan Faces Shortages of Cooking Oil and Poultry Amidst Restrictions
item.description: Private shops in Turkmenistan's Mary region have stopped selling cooking oil, while queues form for chicken. State stores offer limited quantities of one liter of oil and one kilogram of chicken per family. Despite official claims of stable prices and availability, reports indicate poor quality products and high demand due to affordability issues.

item.title: Central Asian power grid failure causes Bishkek electricity outages
item.description: Parts of Bishkek experienced power outages on September 25 due to an emergency shutdown of generation capacity in Uzbekistan. The disruption affected the north-south transmission link. The National Electric Network of Kyrgyzstan stated its protection system operated as designed, and the power system is now stable. Investigations into the cause are ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China sign 10 agreements at investment forum in Almaty
item.description: Ten agreements were signed at the "Kazakhstan-China" investment forum in Almaty. Projects include building an electrolytic aluminum plant and a wind power station in the Abai region, a particleboard plant in Semey, and renewable energy projects in Akmola region. Agreements also cover establishing an investment fund and developing high-tech automotive projects.

item.title: Kyrgyz State Secretary Arslan Koichiev meets Kazakhstan Vice President Yerlan Karin
item.description: Kyrgyz State Secretary Arslan Koichiev met with Kazakhstan Vice President Yerlan Karin in Astana. They discussed strengthening bilateral relations and preserving historical, cultural, and humanitarian ties between the two nations. Both sides emphasized the importance of continued mutual support and constructive dialogue to expand societal and humanitarian connections.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Medical Fund Finances 60% of Annual Plan Amid Payment Delays
item.description: Kazakhstan's Medical Insurance Fund (FMS) has disbursed 1.78 trillion tenge for healthcare services, reaching 60% of its annual plan. Delays in payments are attributed to regulatory changes and technical issues with the Ministry of Health's databases. The fund has implemented measures like advance payments to ensure continuous financing for medical organizations.

item.title: Tokayev Discusses Investment Forum with China
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev spoke at the Kazakhstan-China Investment Forum. The specific topics of his address were not detailed in the provided information, but the forum focused on investment opportunities between the two nations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Signs Decree for January 2027 Presidential Elections
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov has signed a decree to ensure free, fair, and transparent presidential elections scheduled for January 27, 2027. The decree aims to uphold legality, transparency, citizens' electoral rights, and equal conditions for all candidates.

item.title: Differences in cars of the same model purchased in Europe, China, and Kazakhstan
item.description: Cars of the same model purchased in Europe, China, and Kazakhstan differ significantly due to varying national standardization and certification requirements. European standards mandate specific control units, unlike cheaper Chinese alternatives, impacting final prices. Chinese vehicles often have lower body galvanization due to milder winters.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China establish joint investment fund to attract capital
item.description: Kazakhstan and China are creating a joint investment fund to finance major projects, aiming to attract Chinese companies as long-term investors. Cooperation will focus on transport, industrial interaction with a $62 billion project portfolio, and digitalization. Kazakhstan seeks to streamline the investment cycle.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Adopting a New Criminal Code After 105 Amendments
item.description: Kazakhstan is evaluating the necessity of a new Criminal Code, considering the 105 amendments made to the existing one over the past decade. The discussion centers on whether the current legal framework adequately addresses contemporary challenges or if a comprehensive revision is required.
